name: Highlands 2

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a single-story residence situated on a large, open desert scrubland parcel with sparse juniper vegetation distributed across the surrounding terrain|A circular or looped driveway is visible directly around the structure, connecting to a single paved access road that curves from the south and appears to link to the main road network visible at the bottom-right of the image|The structure itself is relatively compact, with a tan or earth-toned roof, and is set back significantly from the road, requiring travel along an extended private drive|No fencing, gates, outbuildings, or pools are visible on this parcel; the surrounding land is open and largely undeveloped desert terrain.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from an oblique angle, revealing the residence positioned centrally on the parcel with desert scrubland extending broadly in all directions|A light-colored circular driveway or apron is visible around the front of the structure, with the access road extending toward the front of the parcel|Scattered juniper trees are distributed across the terrain between the structure and the road, but none are in close contact with the building|The front facade shows a low-profile, single-story form with a dark roof section visible.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, with the residence visible near the center of the parcel surrounded by the circular driveway|The terrain on the right side of the property is open, flat-to-gently-rolling desert with scattered juniper vegetation and no fencing or barriers|The paved access road is visible running along the lower portion of this view, connecting toward the main road|No outbuildings or secondary structures are visible on this side of the parcel.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, where the residence is visible with open desert terrain extending broadly behind it|Several juniper trees are clustered near and immediately behind the structure, providing the densest vegetation observed around the building from any view|The paved access driveway curves away from the rear of the property toward the road|No outbuildings, fencing, pools, or utility infrastructure are visible at the rear.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with the residence visible toward the upper-right of the frame and a long, curved light-colored road or track visible along the left edge of the parcel|The terrain on this side is open desert scrubland with scattered junipers and no fencing, walls, or secondary structures|The road trace visible on this side connects toward the main access road network at the south end of the parcel|The left side of the structure shows a dark, flat or low-pitched roof form.

considerations: The residence is accessed via a single extended paved private driveway that loops around the structure, providing a turnaround capability for emergency vehicles. The parcel is surrounded by open desert terrain with no fencing or gates observed, allowing off-road foot approach from multiple directions. Juniper trees are clustered closest to the rear of the structure, which is the side most obscured from the road approach. The significant setback from the public road means extended hose lays or prolonged apparatus positioning on the private drive should be anticipated.
clarifications: Is the private access driveway constructed to a surface weight rating suitable for heavy emergency apparatus? Are there any locked gates or access control measures at the driveway entrance from the public road that are not visible in the imagery? Are any propane or other fuel storage tanks present on the property that are not visible from the aerial views? Does the structure have a basement or below-grade spaces that would affect interior access?
